candidates.name: West-East Pipeline (ADNOC Hormuz-bypass, Jebel Dhanna/Habshan-Fujairah)

values.OtherEnglishNames: West to East Pipeline (WEP); ADNOC Hormuz Bypass Pipeline; West-East 1 Pipeline; Jebel Dhanna–Fujairah Oil Pipeline
values.RouteType: Not mapped (but could be — route or endpoints are known)
values.RouteNotes: Endpoints and mid-route pump stations are corroborated across independent sources but no GIS/GeoJSON exists yet, so RouteAccuracy=low (known endpoints only). Route runs Jebel Dhanna storage facility (west, Abu Dhabi) -> Habshan (Main Pumping Station, per EPC-subcontractor MFEC) -> Sweihan (Intermediate Pumping Station, per MFEC) -> Fujairah Main Oil Terminal (east); MFEC's equipment-award page is the most granular independent confirmation of this west-to-east routing and resolves the Habshan-vs-Jebel-Dhanna-origin ambiguity in the consolidator note: Jebel Dhanna is the true origin, Habshan is an intermediate pump station on the same route (also traversed by the existing, separate ADCOP/P0553 line). Length is reported inconsistently across sources: 520km (MEED, GlobalData/offshore-technology, dmsuniverse), ~500km (Energy Intel), ~499km/310mi (IIR Energy/Industrial Info), vs a 300km outlier (Kpler blog, uncorroborated elsewhere and likely conflating this with a shorter analogous project). Took 520km as the LengthKnown value on 3-source convergence (MEED + GlobalData + dmsuniverse); flagging the low end (~500km) as plausible alternate. Diameter 48in and this pipeline being distinct from (not a debottlenecking of) the existing 1.8mn b/d Bab-Habshan–Fujairah/ADCOP line (P0553, 406km/48in, operating since 2012) are consistent across all sources consulted.

candidates.researcher_notes: New second crude export line, distinct from the existing 1.8mn b/d Bab-Habshan–Fujairah/ADCOP pipeline (GEM P0553, 406km/48in, operating since 2012) which it will parallel to the same Fujairah terminal. Re-checked against discovery_context.json's 47 existing UAE rows first: P0553 and the Bab-Habshan-Jebel Dhanna lines (P0639/P7214/P7215/P7216) are older, already-operating segments with different lengths/diameters/segment counts and none match this project's under-construction, 2027-target, ~520km/48in/1.5mn bpd profile -> classed new_row, not matched_existing. Meets all three add-threshold legs: (a) sponsor ADNOC/ADNOC Onshore, EPC contractor ENPPI (confirmed independently by contractor-side pages mecgroup.ae and mfec.ae, both live and unaffiliated with each other or with ADNOC's own site); (b) country UAE, endpoints Jebel Dhanna (Abu Dhabi) -> Fujairah; (c) concrete step well past MOU stage — EPCM/detailed engineering underway since 2023 (mecgroup), main EPC contract awarded per MEED (Jan/Feb 2024), equipment orders placed (mfec, Dec 2024), and independently reported ~50% physically complete as of May 2026 (industrialinfo, gulfnews) with 2027 startup target repeated across >10 independent 2026 outlets (Al Jazeera, CNBC, Gulf News, The National, JPT/SPE, Oilprice, Egypt Oil & Gas, MEED, Argus, Kpler). Owner/operator entity check: entity_lookup.py confirms 'ADNOC' already exists as an Owner/Parent string in this same UAE sheet (used on Bab-Habshan-Jebel Dhanna and other ADNOC-owned lines) — reused that exact convention (Owner='ADNOC [100.%]', Parent='Abu Dhabi National Oil Co [100.00%]') rather than inventing a new entity string; no dedicated Owner/Parent [ref] column exists in this sheet so sourcing for Owner is carried here rather than as an orphan ref key. Two things flagged for a human pass: (1) route/length reconciliation — see RouteNotes, went with the 520km figure on 3-source convergence over Kpler's 300km outlier and Energy Intel/Industrial Info's ~500km; (2) capacity is reported consistently as 1.5mn b/d *added* capacity (not total) — combined Fujairah bypass capacity once both lines run is ~3.3mn b/d per Argus/CNBC, so Capacity=1,500,000 bpd is this new line's own throughput, not the combined figure. FIDStatus left blank per controlled_vocab.md (only populated when Status=proposed; this is already Status=construction). ProposalYear left blank — no source gives a clean pre-2023 'proposed/announced' date independent of the 2023 EPCM-engineering start already captured in ConstructionYear; did not want to guess a proposal date not in evidence. No non-English-language sourcing was pursued given English trade press (Argus, MEES, MEED, Energy Intel, JPT/SPE) and two independent UAE-based contractor company sites (mecgroup.ae, mfec.ae) already gave strong, mutually-corroborating primary-adjacent detail; tier=high on that basis (>15 independent outlets, 2 independent EPC-subcontractor primary sources, multi-year timeline consistency 2023->2026).
